query: How does the combined detecion of KAI1 and VEGF improve the diagnosis of HCC?
draft_answer: In the provided evidence, only one paper directly addresses KAI1 and VEGF in HCC diagnosis, reporting that serum KAI1 is downregulated while VEGF is upregulated in HCC patients and that each marker has individual diagnostic value [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. The same study found that combining KAI1 and VEGF improved diagnostic performance compared with KAI1 alone, increasing sensitivity from 86.96% to 91.86% and accuracy from 83.06% to 84.68%, with a negative predictive value of 78.79% [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The authors concluded that combined detection may greatly improve the efficiency of HCC diagnosis and could form a reliable panel of diagnostic markers [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. No other provided paper offers supporting evidence about KAI1 and VEGF together in HCC diagnosis, and several summaries explicitly state that they do not mention these markers [pmc_PMC8318739||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9806080||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3178660840||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9805748||ABSTRACT||001]. Therefore, the conclusion rests on a single study and should be treated as suggestive rather than definitive [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001].

key_claims.claim: In HCC patients, serum KAI1 is downregulated and VEGF is upregulated, and each marker has diagnostic value on its own [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000].

Combined detection of KAI1 and VEGF improved diagnostic performance compared with KAI1 alone, raising sensitivity from 86.96% to 91.86% and accuracy from 83.06% to 84.68% [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001].
The combined KAI1/VEGF panel achieved a negative predictive value of 78.79% [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001].
The authors concluded that combined KAI1 and VEGF detection may greatly improve HCC diagnostic efficiency and serve as a reliable diagnostic marker panel [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001].
